method: Each claim checked against the retrieved abstract text of its cited source, not the citation.

claims.source_text: a treat-to-target management strategy with ULT dose titration guided by serial serum urate (SU) measurements, with an SU target of <6 mg/dl

claims.claim: EULAR target <6 mg/dL (360 umol/L), <5 mg/dL (300 umol/L) in severe gout
claims.source_text: serum uric acid (SUA) levels should be maintained at<6 mg/dL (360 µmol/L) and <5 mg/dL (300 µmol/L) in those with severe gout

claims.claim: Flare: colchicine, NSAIDs, oral or intra-articular steroids, or combination
claims.source_text: For the treatment of flare, colchicine, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), oral or intra-articular steroids or a combination are recommended

claims.claim: IL-1 blocker where flares frequent and colchicine/NSAIDs/steroids contraindicated
claims.source_text: In patients with frequent flare and contraindications to colchicine, NSAIDs and corticosteroids, an interleukin-1 blocker should be considered

claims.source_text: allopurinol as the preferred first-line ULT, including for those with moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease (CKD; stage >3)

claims.claim: Low starting dose: allopurinol <=100 mg/day (lower in CKD), febuxostat <40 mg/day
claims.source_text: using a low starting dose of allopurinol (<=100 mg/day, and lower in CKD) or febuxostat (<40 mg/day)

claims.claim: Initiate ULT for tophaceous gout, radiographic damage, or frequent flares
claims.source_text: initiation of ULT for all patients with tophaceous gout, radiographic damage due to gout, or frequent gout flares

claims.claim: EULAR: ULT considered from first presentation
claims.source_text: urate-lowering therapy (ULT) should be considered from the first presentation of the disease

claims.claim: Anti-inflammatory prophylaxis at least 3-6 months when starting ULT
claims.source_text: concomitant antiinflammatory prophylaxis therapy for a duration of at least 3-6 months was strongly recommended
